newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee trade quiet ahead of new harvest.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee trade quiet ahead of new harvest.

text.p: Vietnam robusta coffee prices remained stable this week in quiet trade, but dealers said on Friday they expected prices to come under pressure over the next few months.
They said coffee was trading at $1,220-$1,250 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, unchanged from a week earlier.

"But we may see lower prices and differentials over the next few months," said a trader. "The Indonesian and Brazil crops are good and Vietnam's is also large. There may be a struggle then to sell coffee."
While accurate figures are not available Vietnam is believed to have exported around 230,000 tonnes from its 1995/96 harvest.
Although beans from the new harvest in Dong Nai province have begun appearing, output from the main producing area in Dak Lak is not expected to arrive for several weeks.
Estimates for the new crop currently stand at 270,000 tonnes.
